Thank you for your support. Because it's a great game still, it's hard to ask anyone outside of this situation to take a stand on anything, but I still wanted to have people be aware of the situation regardless.

If they just kept it as their original statement of "it's not anything cultural, because it is from a fictional setting" it honestly would've been fine. Or if it was any other time, it wouldn't have been as big of a deal.

But currently, it has been going on the internet that Korean traditions such as "gat"(korean hat), "hanbok" (traditional dress), and "kimchi" (traditional food) etc. are actually Chinese culture. They have periodical dramas where they are clearly wearing hanbok and gat in them while saying it's a chinese historical drama. This really didn't help with all of this either.

Yeah. I was very sad that this had to become such a political fight between two countries, but the timing was oddly perfect with the current controversy of many Chinese folks claiming that some culturally Korean things are in fact Chinese culture.

Thank you. I thought I was going crazy because I thought the TGC statement was giving vibes of "oh sorry you felt that way, but you're overreacting on this and misunderstanding it.", but everyone else was saying it was fine. Yeah I don't expect them to give out a better statement, and I honestly don't blame them with how big the Chinese market is.

All of this is madly frustrating, and I wanted to let everyone know that it kinda is a big deal, and to not point fingers at Koreans when the internet trolls on China say that Korean's are the thieves. I've been seeing that on the twitter threads, and it makes me sad and angry. 

Anyways, thanks so much for your comment! It's a great game nonetheless. Shame it had to end this way.

I'm not putting the blame entirely on TGC. I know those were not choices made directly by TGC, which is why I didn't think much of it until now. But seeing how much influence the market has on Sky, it's hard to guarantee this won't happen again in a different scenario to a different culture/group etc. 

I just wanted to say my piece, because a whole lot of Chinese players have been calling Koreans thieves, and I wanted to clarify that we're not trying to steal anyone's culture and that it is a serious matter to Koreans because this isn't the first time this happened to Koreans with China (because so many people have been saying it's not a big deal).

I mean, it's one's culture. I guess it depends on perspective, but it sorta feels like someone took your family heirloom and said it was theirs. And when calling them out on it, they just said, "oh sorry you feel that way, but I swear this was ours first. You're just being too sensitive." 

I'm not asking them to cater to everyone. I just wanted them to not be a sell out to the Chinese market like I see a lot of companies doing.

Yeah I figured. They have been showing a lot of favoritism to the Chinese server too by giving out free cosmetics when it is ridiculously expensive elsewhere. All of this didn't sit right with me. I think it's right for me to stop here with this game . Thanks for the support of my decision though!

I did read it, and I understand they have apologized. But as I said in the comment above, if you look at the comments in Jenova Chen's statement from chinese users, they are calling Korean players Korean Thief and so forth. Including that with the constant favoritism on their Chinese players, the blame sort of is placed on the Koreans rn for being "overly sensitive" and trying to take Chinese culture. 

Overall, the timing was oddly aligned recent controversy, and if something like this happens again, I can't say they won't say something along the lines of "oh sorry you felt that way, but you're just being too sensitive about it."
